# 1. Introduction

Can five gene mutation indicators help tell lower-grade glioma (LGG)
and glioblastoma (GBM) apart better than age alone? I used the
prepared UCI glioma dataset to compare two logistic regression models.

- Model A uses age at diagnosis.
- Model B uses age and mutation status for IDH1, TP53, ATRX, EGFR and PTEN.

# 2. Setup

```{r setup}
# Load the plotting package.
library(ggplot2)
grade_colors <- c(LGG = "#E76F51", GBM = "#008C95")

# Identify the RStudio project folder.
root <- here::here()

# Create paths for folders.
data_dir <- file.path(root, "data")
fig_dir <- file.path(root, "figures")
results_dir <- file.path(root, "results")

# Ensure output folders exist.
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# R Markdown settings.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE
)
```

# 3. Data Import

```{r import-data}
# Location of the official preprocessed UCI dataset.
input_file <- file.path(
  data_dir,
  "TCGA_InfoWithGrade.csv"
)

# Give a clear error if the file is missing.
if (!file.exists(input_file)) {
  stop("Place TCGA_InfoWithGrade.csv inside the data folder.")
}

# Import the CSV file with its header.
raw <- read.csv(input_file, check.names = FALSE)

# All 20 gene columns from the original dataset.
genes <- c(
  "IDH1", "TP53", "ATRX", "PTEN", "EGFR",
  "CIC", "MUC16", "PIK3CA", "NF1", "PIK3R1",
  "FUBP1", "RB1", "NOTCH1", "BCOR", "CSMD3",
  "SMARCA4", "GRIN2A", "IDH2", "FAT4", "PDGFRA"
)

# Check the expected original column names.
expected_columns <- c(
  "Grade",
  "Gender",
  "Age_at_diagnosis",
  "Race",
  genes
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(raw) == 839,
  ncol(raw) == 24,
  identical(names(raw), expected_columns)
)

# Examine the imported data.
dim(raw)
head(raw)
str(raw)
summary(raw)
```

# 4. Data Quality Control and Preprocessing

```{r cleaning}
# Count missing values.
missing_values <- sum(is.na(raw))
cat("Missing values:", missing_values, "\n")

# Check for identical complete rows.
duplicate_rows <- sum(duplicated(raw))
cat("Identical rows:", duplicate_rows, "\n")

# Confirm numerical column types.
numeric_columns <- c(
  "Grade", "Age_at_diagnosis", genes
)

stopifnot(all(vapply(
  raw[numeric_columns],
  is.numeric,
  logical(1)
)))

# Check the target uses the documented coding.
stopifnot(all(raw$Grade %in% c(0, 1)))

# Check mutation indicators only contain 0 or 1.
for (gene in genes) {
  stopifnot(all(raw[[gene]] %in% c(0, 1)))
}

# The official preprocessed dataset should be complete.
if (missing_values > 0) {
  stop("Unexpected missing data found.")
}

# Keep the original numeric target for modelling.
df <- raw

# Add readable labels for graphs and summaries.
df$GradeLabel <- factor(
  df$Grade,
  levels = c(0, 1),
  labels = c("LGG", "GBM")
)

# Save a copy with the additional readable label.
write.csv(
  df,
  file.path(data_dir, "cleaned_glioma.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Count LGG and GBM records.
table(df$GradeLabel)

# Display class proportions.
prop.table(table(df$GradeLabel))
```

## 5.3 Mutation Frequencies for All 20 Genes

```{r mutation-frequency}
# Calculate the percentage of mutated samples
# separately in each glioma class for every gene.

mutation_rates <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(genes, function(gene) {

    lgg_rate <- mean(
      df[[gene]][df$GradeLabel == "LGG"]
    ) * 100

    gbm_rate <- mean(
      df[[gene]][df$GradeLabel == "GBM"]
    ) * 100

    data.frame(
      Gene = gene,
      Grade = factor(c("LGG", "GBM"), levels = c("LGG", "GBM")),
      MutationPercent = c(lgg_rate, gbm_rate)
    )
  })
)

# Display the percentage table.
head(mutation_rates, 10)

# Save the table.
write.csv(
  mutation_rates,
  file.path(results_dir, "mutation_frequencies.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Plot mutations for all 20 genes.
p3 <- ggplot(
  mutation_rates,
  aes(
    x = Gene,
    y = MutationPercent,
    fill = Grade
  )
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Mutation Frequency by Glioma Class",
    x = "Gene",
    y = "Mutated Samples (%)",
    fill = "Glioma Class"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = grade_colors) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p3)

ggsave(
  file.path(fig_dir, "03_mutation_frequency.png"),
  plot = p3,
  width = 10,
  height = 9,
  dpi = 150
)
```

# 6. Statistical Analysis

## 6.1 IDH1 Mutation and Glioma Class

```{r idh1-test}
# Create a contingency table.
idh1_table <- table(
  Grade = df$GradeLabel,
  IDH1_Mutation = df$IDH1
)

idh1_table

# Test whether IDH1 mutation status and
# the glioma class are statistically associated.
idh1_test <- fisher.test(idh1_table)

# Display the p-value and odds-ratio estimate.
idh1_test
cat("Exact p-value:", format(idh1_test$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
```

# 7. Machine Learning

## 7.1 Split Into Training and Testing Data

```{r data-split}
# Set a fixed random seed for reproducibility.
set.seed(123)

# Find row indices for each class.
lgg_ids <- which(df$Grade == 0)
gbm_ids <- which(df$Grade == 1)

# Select approximately 80% within each class.
train_lgg <- sample(
  lgg_ids,
  floor(0.8 * length(lgg_ids))
)

train_gbm <- sample(
  gbm_ids,
  floor(0.8 * length(gbm_ids))
)

# Combine selected indices.
train_ids <- sort(c(train_lgg, train_gbm))

# Create independent training and test subsets.
train <- df[train_ids, ]
test <- df[-train_ids, ]

# Verify their sizes.
cat("Training samples:", nrow(train), "\n")
cat("Testing samples:", nrow(test), "\n")

# Display the class distribution in each subset.
table(train$GradeLabel)
table(test$GradeLabel)

stopifnot(nrow(train) == 670)
stopifnot(nrow(test) == 169)
```

## 7.2 Model A: Age Only

```{r age-model}
# Logistic regression using just age.
model_age <- glm(
  Grade ~ Age_at_diagnosis,
  data = train,
  family = binomial()
)

# Inspect fitted coefficients.
summary(model_age)
```

## 7.3 Model B: Age and Selected Gene Mutations

The model uses IDH1, TP53 and ATRX, which were more often mutated in LGG, and EGFR and PTEN, which were more often mutated in GBM. This gives the model a small set of genes with patterns in both groups.

```{r full-model}
# The second model uses age and five genes.
# Mutation columns are binary indicators (0 or 1).

model_genes <- glm(
  Grade ~ Age_at_diagnosis +
    IDH1 +
    TP53 +
    ATRX +
    EGFR +
    PTEN,
  data = train,
  family = binomial()
)

# View coefficients and statistical information.
summary(model_genes)
```

## 7.4 Generate Test Predictions

```{r predictions}
# Predict probabilities of GBM for the test set.

prob_age <- predict(
  model_age,
  newdata = test,
  type = "response"
)

prob_genes <- predict(
  model_genes,
  newdata = test,
  type = "response"
)

# Confirm probabilities are valid.
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(prob_age)),
  all(is.finite(prob_genes)),
  all(prob_age >= 0 & prob_age <= 1),
  all(prob_genes >= 0 & prob_genes <= 1)
)

# Display some predicted probabilities.
head(prob_genes)
```

# 8. Model Evaluation

## 8.1 Evaluation Function

```{r evaluation-function}
# This function calculates performance for either model.
# The positive class is GBM.

evaluate_model <- function(actual, probabilities, name) {

  # Convert probabilities into 0/1 predictions.
  predicted <- ifelse(probabilities >= 0.5, 1, 0)

  # Create confusion matrix with a fixed class order.
  cm <- table(
    Actual = factor(
      actual,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("LGG", "GBM")
    ),
    Predicted = factor(
      predicted,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("LGG", "GBM")
    )
  )

  # Extract confusion matrix components.
  TP <- cm["GBM", "GBM"]
  TN <- cm["LGG", "LGG"]
  FP <- cm["LGG", "GBM"]
  FN <- cm["GBM", "LGG"]

  # Avoid division-by-zero errors.
  safe_divide <- function(a, b) {
    if (b == 0) return(NA_real_)
    a / b
  }

  # Calculate metrics.
  accuracy <- safe_divide(TP + TN, sum(cm))
  precision <- safe_divide(TP, TP + FP)
  recall <- safe_divide(TP, TP + FN)
  specificity <- safe_divide(TN, TN + FP)

  # Calculate the F1-score.
  if (
    is.na(precision) ||
    is.na(recall) ||
    precision + recall == 0
  ) {
    f1 <- NA_real_
  } else {
    f1 <- 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
  }

  # Return evaluation results.
  list(
    confusion = cm,
    metrics = data.frame(
      Model = name,
      Accuracy = round(accuracy, 4),
      Precision = round(precision, 4),
      Recall = round(recall, 4),
      Specificity = round(specificity, 4),
      F1 = round(f1, 4)
    )
  )
}
```

## 8.2 Evaluate Both Models

```{r model-comparison}
# Evaluate baseline age-only model.
eval_age <- evaluate_model(
  test$Grade,
  prob_age,
  "Age only"
)

# Evaluate age + mutation model.
eval_genes <- evaluate_model(
  test$Grade,
  prob_genes,
  "Age + 5 genes"
)

# Combine metric tables.
comparison <- rbind(
  eval_age$metrics,
  eval_genes$metrics
)

# Display and save the comparison.
knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 4)

write.csv(
  comparison,
  file.path(results_dir, "model_comparison.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## 8.3 Confusion Matrix for Main Model

```{r confusion-matrix}
# Print the actual and predicted classes.
eval_genes$confusion

# Save the matrix as a CSV file.
write.csv(
  as.data.frame.matrix(eval_genes$confusion),
  file.path(results_dir, "confusion_matrix.csv")
)
```

# 9. What the results show

IDH1 mutations were much more common in the LGG group. Fisher's
exact test shows an association between IDH1 status and recorded grade.

On the same 169 test cases, the age-only model got 123 right and the
age-plus-five-gene model got 145 right. The second model found 64 of
71 GBM cases, compared with 48 for age alone.

This comparison uses one split of a historical dataset. Testing on a
separate dataset would help show whether the results hold elsewhere.
